Do his gyrations actually improve his balance? It seems like eventually you would find an equilibrium and be still, but he doesn't. Instead of constant corrections, he seems to be making patterned moves in their place. Is this his secret? He's not reacting to his loss of balance with counter weight and thus risking over correction. He's intentionally moving in a rhythmic pattern as a way as to not loose balance in the first place.

The rhythm is easier than trying to achieve the impossible of a perfect balance. If you try to achieve perfect balance you will inevitably start to drift some direction but your body won't be able to detect it easily and so you would still be making a series of corrections but each one would be "random" and you would have to determine the direction and velocity of the movement and correct it.

With a set rhythm you know the direction and approximate velocity of your next move and the one that follows. Any correction for the imperfections can be incorporated as a change in the velocity only and he can probably go through several iteration of the pattern uncorrected with little harm. Also there should be some degree of self correction i.e. if he is moving too fast one direction, that "excess" is stopped and reset such that he is almost working from a clean slate each iteration.

TLDR - It is much easier to practice controlled imperfection than to try to practice all the ways perfection can fail.
